tools.name: get_test_key
tools.description: Self-issue a SEALED-tier Witness API key IN-BAND (no human, no signup page). Sealed tier is FREE and includes 5,000 seals/month (measured + surfaced on every seal, NEVER blocked over the limit; billing is not yet live). Records are Ed25519-signed + hash-chained + independently verifiable OFFLINE, but NOT externally anchored — so "provable even against VDA" does NOT apply, and that is terminal on this tier (a Sealed record stays sealed). Pass controllerPublicKeyJwk (an Ed25519 public JWK you hold) to CLAIM a DURABLE account you can self-renew forever via renew_challenge/renew_key — otherwise it auto-expires ~7 days. `verify` needs no key; use this key to `seal`. The Anchored tier (externally committed — provable even against us — from EUR 50/mo) is concierge-provisioned on request (enabled manually today), and upgrading preserves your account id + chains. Same hardened anonymous-mint caps as the REST endpoint (global 500/day, per-IP, kill switch).

controllerPublicKeyJwk.description: Optional Ed25519 public JWK {kty:'OKP',crv:'Ed25519',x} — bind to claim a durable, self-renewable account

tools.name: renew_challenge
tools.description: Step 1 of agent-provable, no-human key renewal for an EXISTING durable account. Returns a one-time nonce. Then Ed25519-sign the exact string "vda.witness.renew/1|<accountId>|<nonce>" with your controller key and call renew_key. Only an account bound to a controller key (see get_test_key controllerPublicKeyJwk) can complete renewal.

tools.name: renew_key
tools.description: Step 2 of agent-provable renewal: prove control of your account by signing the challenge nonce with your controller key, and receive a FRESH short-TTL API key bound to the SAME account (same chains continue; prior keys stay valid until they expire — no seal gap). No human, no standing secret. This is how a short-lived key stops being a death sentence.

tools.name: seal
tools.description: General-purpose seal (compatibility / unstructured). Prefer a SHAPED skill so your record is auditor-reconstructable: seal_hitl_decision (a human decided), seal_agent_action (an autonomous agent acted), or seal_attestation (you assert a fact/state). This generic seal is retained for backward compatibility and for records that fit none of those; its records carry no record_type and report as unstructured. Requires a Witness API key. The response carries a `usage` headroom block; over the included allowance it WARNS but never blocks.

ruleText.description: The governing rule verbatim or a stable reference

chainKey.description: Optional per-(account,chain) ordering namespace; default 'default'. This is ALSO the GROUPING primitive: records sharing a chainKey are hash-linked into one retrievable, independently-provable set — GET /chains/<chainKey>/proof returns the whole trail in one call and /report scopes to it. To group the seals of one workflow/bundle/case, give them a stable shared chainKey (e.g. 'c2md:bundle:<id>') — do NOT invent a grouping field inside your own payloads. Max 128 chars [A-Za-z0-9._:-]

decisionId.description: Optional idempotency key; dedupe on (account, decisionId)

tools.name: seal_hitl_decision
tools.description: Seal a governance record for a HUMAN-IN-THE-LOOP decision. A correct HITL record is content-based: it captures the deciding human's identity and role, the disposition and its rationale, the policies/SOPs cited AS THE BASIS (by reference, and where possible captured text or hash — policies change, and an auditor needs the version in force), and content-addressable references (with sha256 hashes) to the system-of-record artifacts the decider SAW at decision time (reservation records, folios, inventory state) — NOT the action the decision produced. This makes the sealed trail auditor-reconstructable: from the record alone, an auditor can verify exactly what state the decider was looking at. Witness seals the ASSERTED identity of the actor; it does not independently authenticate them. Embed artifacts via evidence[].inline when upstream availability isn't guaranteed (≤100KB; Witness verifies bytes against the hash). If a decision legitimately has no evidentiary basis, state why in evidence_omitted_reason — do not omit it silently. Requires a Witness API key.

type.description: Must be 'human' — for machine decisions use seal_agent_action

role.description: Optional — the authority under which they decided

disposition.description: Recommended controlled outcome, e.g. approved / rejected / escalated / modified

ref.description: Policy / SOP / rule identifier (id / URI / path)

text.description: The clause verbatim — policies drift; capture what it SAID at decision time

hash.description: sha256:<hex> of the policy source version

governing_clauses.description: The policies/SOPs/rules cited as the basis (≥1)

ref.description: Content-addressable reference to an EXTERNAL system-of-record artifact (URI / id / a Witness recordId)

hash.description: sha256:<hex> of the artifact — what makes the reference tamper-evident even if `ref` later rots or is swapped

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 when this artifact was captured

inline.description: Embed the artifact verbatim (≤100KB decoded) when upstream availability isn't guaranteed; Witness verifies the bytes hash to `hash` at seal time and rejects a mismatch

evidence.description: External system-of-record artifacts the decider SAW (≥1, or give evidence_omitted_reason)

evidence_omitted_reason.description: Required only if evidence is empty — why this decision has no evidentiary basis

basis_captured_at.description: ISO-8601 — when the evidentiary basis was captured (decision time, NOT seal time)

decision_context.description: Optional freeform notes on the decision session

chainKey.description: Optional per-(account,chain) ordering namespace; default 'default'. tools.name: seal_agent_action
tools.description: Seal a record for an action taken AUTONOMOUSLY by an agent under a governing rule. Captures the acting agent's identity, the governing rule, and what the agent CONSUMED to act — as two distinct fields by provenance: `evidence` is EXTERNAL material it saw (content-addressed + hashed — e.g. a whoami response from another service, a fetched record), `parameters` is the COMPUTED arguments it was passed (self-contained here, no hash — e.g. requested scopes, jurisdictions, data categories). Populate one or both; a record must record at least one (or give evidence_omitted_reason). The one-question test: does it exist outside this record? → evidence (hash it). Did you compute/pass it as an argument? → parameters. Optionally include agent_context (free-form execution-substrate hints like cloud_run_revision, model_name, region) so an auditor can ask 'was this at a known-buggy revision?' — asserted by you, not verified by Witness. For a human decision use seal_hitl_decision. Requires a Witness API key.

tools.name: seal_attestation

Optionally cite the framework it's made under via governing_basis; otherwise it is sealed as attested-by-the-signing-party, not independently verified by Witness. Requires a Witness API key.

tools.name: issue_admission_credential
tools.description: Issue an agent ADMISSION CREDENTIAL — a sealed attestation admitting an agent (subject_did) to a customer environment with a scope, valid until expiry. The credential IS the Witness record; enforcers check it by id via verify_admission_credential, and it is revocable via revoke_admission_credential. Sealed by YOUR account (the issuer) — only your account can later revoke it. subject_did / environment_id / scope / compliance_mappings are ASSERTED, not authenticated by Witness. Requires a Witness API key.

issuer_did.description: The issuer, e.g. did:web:onboard.getvda.ai (asserted; issuer authority derives from your sealing account)

environment_id.description: The customer environment this credential admits to (single; multi-env = multiple credentials)

governance_files_hash.description: Content hash of the sealed governance file set the agent was admitted with

pass.description: false is valid — an honest non-passing / provisional admission

evidence_seal_ref.description: Witness recordId of the sealed sandbox evidence (may be an honest stub record)

impact_delta_ref.description: Witness recordId (seal ref) of the accepted impact-delta report

tools.name: check_valid
tools.description: Is this admission credential currently valid? Given credential_id, returns the single canonical verdict computed by Witness — issued ∧ signature verifies ∧ not revoked by the issuer ∧ not expired — so every enforcer is identically correct and the meaning of 'valid' evolves in one place, never drifting across independent implementations. Response: {valid, code, subject, issuer, environment, scope, expires_at, revoked, revoked_at?, reason_code?}, where code is 'valid' | 'revoked' | 'expired' | 'not_found' | 'not_credential'. PUBLIC — no key (a credential id is not a secret and grants no capability; same posture as a PKI CRL/OCSP endpoint). Cache ~60s; revocations propagate within that window. TWO enforcer disciplines: (1) a credential id is a BEARER handle — a valid credential is necessary, NOT sufficient; you MUST separately challenge the presenter to prove control of `subject` (a DID challenge), because verifying validity is not proof the presenter is the subject. (2) Record each check_valid response in YOUR OWN audit log (timestamp, credential_id, response) — Witness's cache and logs tell you what was returned, but only your local record proves what YOU acted on and when, if a regulator later asks how you knew the credential was valid at time T.

tools.name: revoke_admission_credential
tools.description: Revoke an admission credential YOUR account issued. Terminal (re-admission = a new credential). Only the issuing account may revoke. Produces a new immutable revocation attestation superseding the credential; verify_admission_credential reflects it within the ~60s cache window. Requires a Witness API key (the issuer's).

tools.name: verify
tools.description: Independently verify a Witness record or chain (Ed25519 signature + hash-chain integrity). No auth required — keyless.

record.description: A single witness record (including its proof)

records.description: A chain of witness records, in order

tools.name: report
tools.description: Generate an EU AI Act Article 12 EVIDENCE REPORT (a compliance artefact, not an operational query — to read your records use list_records / get_record) from your sealed trail. Scopable by chainKey + date range. Requires a Witness API key.

chainKey.description: Optional — scope the report to one chain

tools.name: list_records
tools.description: List YOUR OWN sealed records (operational query — this is how you read back what you've written). Account-scoped: the account comes from your key, never a parameter. Returns a summary per record (recordId, chainKey, seq, verdict, agent, ruleId, bodyHash, sealedAt, anchorState) plus the set of chainKeys in your account so you can discover your own chains. Paginated (limit + opaque cursor); optional chainKey and since/until (ISO-8601) filters. For full reasoning/inputs of a record, call get_record. Requires a Witness API key.

tools.name: get_record
tools.description: Fetch ONE of your own records by recordId — the FULL signed body: decision{agent, verdict, reasoning, inputs, actionProposed}, governingRule{ruleId, ruleText}, chainKey, seq, prevHash, bodyHash, signer/custodyClaim, proof, plus anchorState and any external anchor. This is how you read back your own reasoning AND get everything needed to verify offline. Account-scoped: a foreign or unknown recordId returns not-found (no existence leak). Requires a Witness API key.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Resolve the presented Witness API key to its identity — the SANCTIONED cross-service authorization endpoint (Contract A). A sibling getvda.ai service that receives `Authorization: Bearer wtn.<id>.<secret>` from ITS caller validates it by calling this (Witness is the sole source of truth for its own keys). Returns { account_id, tier ('SEALED'|'ANCHORED'), scopes, compliance, key_id, revoked:false, expires_at } — everything needed to authorize on identity: WHO (account_id), WHAT TIER, WHAT SCOPES, and VALIDITY (expires_at; revoked keys 401 before reaching here). Takes the caller's own Bearer key (no argument). A key can only ever resolve ITSELF — it cannot enumerate other accounts. Any invalid/missing key returns a uniform 401 'unknown or invalid API key' (no existence leak).

tools.name: verify_record_issuer
tools.description: Is a record's signature by the issuer it claims? Given record_id, returns issuer-authenticity for ANY record — WITHOUT exposing the record. The answer is a verdict + the issuer DID + the public key it resolved against, NEVER decision.inputs, evidence, or body content. Response: { record_id, signature_valid, issuer_verified, issuer_verification, issuer_did, signer_key }. issuer_verification has the same four states as check_valid's: 'verified' (the signing key IS published in the claimed issuer's did:web) | 'key_not_in_did_doc' (LOUD — signed by a key NOT in that DID; suspicious) | 'custodial' (Witness's own key signed it — issuer-authenticity is not the applicable question) | 'did_unresolvable' (the issuer DID could not be resolved — the check did NOT complete; treat as neither verified nor forged). PUBLIC — no key. This is how an enforcer of a privilege-widening event (e.g. a genesis authority registration a service seals about itself) confirms the issuer signed it, not merely that Witness recorded it — without holding the account's key or seeing the record. ids are unguessable UUIDs; unknown → not_found.
